method: Diff-scoped round: the sentences gate scope listed since round 2, plus any chart text changed by code alone. Every non-confirmed verdict was re-checked by an independent skeptic; a finding the skeptic did not uphold is recorded CONFIRMED with both pieces of evidence.

findings.evidence: S: What holds: the 23 files match 'git ls-files --others --exclude-standard rent-vs-buy', and the vet list sits in the ignored draft/. The quoted README statements exist (data/README.md:23, :36, :311, :341, :342, :373, :374, :376; draft :108) and hold literally: no data file is committed, and no ICI or NAIC table appears in any committed file. My scripts read the raw ICI, AEI, PMMS and French files and the NAIC report texts and compare them with all committed text files and the 22,187 numeric leaves of results.json (scan_runs2.py, year_runs.py, scan_results.py, guard_replay.py). They find no run of ICI expense ratios, AEI workbook cells, Freddie Mac weekly values or French monthly factors. results.json holds only derived annual series, and its few exact equalities with source cells are coincidences such as rules.sell_share. The four charts show model output only. The universal 'no table or series ... no run of ... NAIC Table 4 cells' fails in two committed files. (a) docs/round2-verdicts.json:143 (r2:extra:S0 skeptic evidence) quotes six NAIC Table 4 cells: two 2023 HO-3 totals in one sentence, then a four-value 'Spot values' list. My script finds all six on Table 4 pages of the stored reports (2023 text lines 12040, 12060, 12794, 12812; 2022 line 12782; 2021 line 10314). Three of them are the countrywide HO-3 exposure for 2021, 2022 and 2023, a series rather than an individual figure. (b) Design section 7 (:369-371) gives Freddie Mac's published annual averages for each year 1972 to 1977 and 2019 to 2021, plus annual points for 1972 and 2019 to 2021: thirteen figures with consecutive runs. The rates equal the stored weekly file's calendar-year means rounded to 2 decimals (pmms_annual.py). The points do not, so they come from Freddie Mac's annual table. Freddie Mac's terms allow attributed use (provenance-audit.md:74-76), so this breaks the round's rule, not Freddie Mac's terms. Section 7 (:378-380) also reproduces 'as printed' the whole Difference column of DLM's Table 2, all seven non-NA cells (sources/dlm_roiw_2008-13.txt:230-279, a copyrighted article per :48-50). Note: design :391 and :244 cite four individual ICI values as 'ICI' with the report title (:90) but without the http://www.ici.org URL that ICI's citation permission asks for (sources/ici_copyright_linking_ia20260514103053.txt:682). data/README.md:342-349 gives the name and URL for the folder. My evidence cites these figures by locator only, because this record is committed. | skeptic S: upheld: The file list holds: git ls-files --others --exclude-standard rent-vs-buy gives exactly these 23 files, and draft/vet-values-seen.txt is ignored by .gitignore:12. The opening universal fails as worded; figures are cited here by locator only. (1) Design section 7 (:368-371) gives Freddie Mac's discontinued annual averages for each year 1972 to 1977 and 2019 to 2021, plus annual fees and points for 1972 and 2019 to 2021. On a copy of the pinned weekly workbook (sha256 3066c422..., scripts/pmms_means.py), the nine rates equal the calendar-year means of the weekly values rounded to 2 decimals. The 2019 to 2021 points do not, so they come from Freddie Mac's annual table. (2) Design :378-380 reproduces 'as printed' both Difference columns of DLM's Table 2, all seven non-NA cells (sources/dlm_roiw_2008-13.txt:230-279; copyright notice at :48-50). (3) docs/round2-verdicts.json:143 holds six NAIC figures. I found each in the stored reports, after their Table 4 headings: the 2023 text at :12040, :12060, :12794 and :12812 (heading :12004), the 2022 text at :12782 (heading :11994) and the 2021 text at :10314 (heading :9733). Three of them are the HO-3 total exposure for 2021 to 2023. This is the weakest case, since six spot values are close to individual figures. (4) A correction to the finding: results.json does not hold only derived series. Its inputs.value.index equals the pinned FHFA all-transactions file in 204 of 216 quarters, 1975Q1 to 2025Q4 (scripts/fhfa_in_results.py). FHFA allows this use, so only the universal's wording is affected. What holds, on my own scan: scripts/run_scan.py, self-tested on planted runs, finds no run of 3 or more consecutive AEI 'rent-price data' cells, ICI figure columns or rows, PMMS weekly rates or points, or French monthly factors in the 18 committed text files other than results.json. Its only hits are unit-test constants in test_rentbuy.py that match through 2-decimal rounding. In results.json, none of the 12,580 non-integer leaves equals an AEI cell (as is, x100 or /100), and the ICI, PMMS and French equalities are low-precision coincidences such as rules.sell_share, 3.5 and AHS tax rates. The quoted statements (data/README.md:23, :29, :36, :43, :311, :341, :342, :373, :374, :376; draft :108) hold literally. Scripts and input copies are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jonathanchrisnaldy-Claude-Workspace/7a1b9d4a-a613-4eb1-a1d2-f4d11a2b1ecc/scratchpad/p30r3/skeptic-S. | L: The central claim holds on my own scan. lens-L/scripts/extract_sources.py read 337 ICI, 805 AEI and 2,879 Freddie Mac sheet series, plus 8 French factor columns and the 3 NAIC token streams, straight from the raw files. scan_runs.py checked all 19 committed text files for runs of 3 or more consecutive cells (in raw, x100 or /100 form), and I opened all 4 PNGs. No committed file has a run or table of ICI, AEI, Freddie Mac weekly, French monthly or NAIC Table 4 values; every chain found was noise (repeated 100s, property-tax values, line numbers). The same scanner flags 168 real runs in the withdrawn draft/vet-values-seen.txt, so it is sensitive. results.json has 14,398 floats, 0 of which equal an AEI column F ratio or an ICI S3 value /100, and no monthly series (its largest is 216 quarterly FHFA values). Its annual PMMS means and French returns are derived, not copied: the 1990 market return is -6.024 against French's annual -6.05. NAIC appears only as individual figures: 3 form totals at audit:453, and 6 spot values in round2-verdicts

findings.fix_hint: I agree with both parts. (a) Delete '"fund_pct": by_year(fund), ' from annual_returns at build_analysis.py:467. Nothing reads the key, and fund_annualized_pct is computed from the local dict. Delete fund_pct rather than market_pct: French's public factors plus fund_pct alone recover the fee. No other field gives a simple route; the fee sensitivities hold only verdict counts. (b) For AEI, no pure deletion short of chart 1's split_pct removes the encoding, because outlay, payment+carrying, rate_pct+carrying.main and tau+iota+u each rebuild it.
